In all finite verb forms other than the Factual non-Past, the slot -3 (§ sec:outer.prefixal.chain ) is filled, and vowel contraction occurs between the vowel of the preverb and the a- element. The rules of contraction with preverbs are detailed in § sec:preverbs.contracting.verbs, but tab:preverb.contraction presents a summary.

Type C preverbs, which are restricted to transitive verbs, never occur with contracting verbs. In the case of type D preverbs, vowel contraction is avoided by the insertion of the peg circumfix (see § sec:peg.circumfix, § sec:preverbs.contracting.verbs ).

These rules are not purely phonological, since the outcome of the vowel fusion with type A preverbs depends on the TAME category. For instance, in the case of the contracting verb atɤrfall, the type A downwards pɯ- preverbs merges as pɤ- in the Irrealis and Imperative (for example a-mɤ-pɯ-ɤtɤr amɤpɤtɤr in ex:amApAtAr ) and as pa- in the Past Imperfective and Perfective ( pɯ-atɤr patɤr in ex:li.patAr ).

exe

a-mɤ-pɯ-ɤtɤr kɤ-sɯso kɯ, \\
irr - neg - pfv -fall inf -think erg \\
`In order to prevent [the child] from falling down...' (140426 tApAtso kAnWBdaR)
exe

exe

li pɯ-atɤr ɲɯ-ŋu \\
again aor -fall sens -be \\
`He fell down again.' (2003 tWxtsa)
exe

In slot -2, since contracting verbs are all intransitive, only the second person tɯ- and the generic kɯ- prefixes and the prefixal element k(ɯ)- of the peg circumfix can occur before the contracting vowel a-. The outcome of vowel contraction depends on the TAME category (§ sec:intr.23: tɯ-a- ta- in Factual Non-Past ( tɯ-atɤr `you will fall') and Aorist ( pɯ-tɯ-atɤr `you fell down') and tɯ-ɤ- tɤ- Imperfective ( pjɯ-tɯ-ɤtɤr `you fall down'), Sensory, Egophoric Present, Irrealis, Imperative and Prohibitive ( ma-pɯ-tɯ-ɤtɤr `don't fall down'). With the peg circumfix, which appears in the Inferential, the vowel fusion is always -k-ɤ- (see example ex:mWYAkAtWGnWci, § sec:peg.circumfix ).

Slot -1 only contains prefixes associated with transitive verbs, which are therefore incompatible with contracting verbs.

With non-finite verb form prefixes (§ chap:non-finite ), vowel fusion is always ɯ-ɤ / ɤ-ɤ, as summarized in tab:nmlz.contracting.

With inner prefixes, vowel contraction is also straightforward and yields ɤ- in all cases: for instance, the sigmatic causative, applicative and tropative of contracting verbs are sɯ-ɤ- sɤ- (§ sec:caus.sA ), nɯ-ɤ- nɤ- (§ sec:allomorphy.applicative ) and nɤ-ɤ- nɤ- (§ sec:tropative.allomorphy ), respectively. The autive nɯ- cannot undergo vowel fusion and is rather infixed after the contracting vowel a- (§ sec:inner.prefixal.chain, § sec:autoben.position ).

The Progressive prefix asɯ- (§ sec:progressive.morphology ), located in slot -1 (§ sec:outer.prefixal.chain ), can undergo vowel contraction in ways similar to those of contracting verbs, summarized in tab:progressive.contraction. The non-contracting autive nɯ- and inverse -wɣ prefixes are rather infixed between the a- and the -sɯ/z- elements.
summary:
Contracting verbs are morphologically intransitive polysyllabic verbs whose first syllable is a-, and this a- may function as a valency-decreasing, denominal, deideophonic, or unanalyzable prefix. The grammar represents vowel contraction by keeping the prefix in base form and indicating the contracted result after a hyphen, noting that -a, -ɤ-, and -o- are morphologically conditioned allomorphs rather than contrastive vowels.

The passage then describes how contraction works differently across verbal slots and TAME categories: some prefixes merge directly with a-, some do not merge and instead trigger epenthesis or infixation, and certain prefix types are incompatible with contracting verbs. It also notes that the outcomes of contraction are sometimes conditioned by TAME category rather than being purely phonological.

text: Vowel contraction is not restricted to the prefixal verbal template. Nominal stems in a- are extremely few, but do present some instances of vowel contraction (§ sec:a.nouns ). Vowel fusion involving the first person suffixes is discussed in § sec:intr.1.
summary: Vowel contraction is not limited to the prefixal verbal template. Although nominal stems beginning with *a-* are very rare, some do show vowel contraction, and vowel fusion with first-person suffixes is treated elsewhere.

text: reduplication!verb
summary: The passage indicates the topic is reduplication in verbs, but it provides no further details about how the phenomenon works or what linguistic facts are being discussed.

text:
Verb-initial reduplication has a number of morphosyntactic functions, involving clause linking (conditionals § sec:redp.protasis, temporal clauses (§ sec:iterative.coincidence ), expressing increase of degree (§ sec:redp.gradual.increase ), totality (§ sec:totalitative.redp ) or temporal resilience (§ sec:emphatic.autive ). With the possible exception of its use in the protasis of conditionals, all of the functions of the initial reduplication present an iconic component typical of reduplication crosslinguistically.

Initial reduplication belongs to inflectional morphology. The only cases of lexicalization involve grammaticalization of reduplicated finite verb form into a discourse marker (see § sec:delimitative and § sec:redp.protasis below).
summary:
Verb-initial reduplication serves several morphosyntactic functions, including clause linking in conditionals and temporal clauses, and expressing increase of degree, totality, or temporal resilience. Except perhaps in conditional protases, these uses have an iconic component typical of reduplication crosslinguistically.

The passage also states that initial reduplication is part of inflectional morphology, with lexicalization limited to cases where a reduplicated finite verb has grammaticalized into a discourse marker.

text:
While initial reduplication follows the general rules of partial reduplication (§ sec:partial.redp ), two additional rules have to be taken into account.

First, the outcome of the reduplication of the negative prefix mɯ- is mɯ mɤ- with vowel alternation (§ sec:neg.allomorphs ), not distinguishable from that of the prefix mɤ-.

Second, when the initial syllable of the word contains more than one morpheme, as in the case of the ɕ- or ʑ- allomorphs of the translocative prefix combined with an orientation preverb (§ sec:translocative.morpho ), reduplication can disregard morpheme boundaries, resulting in a replication of the two morphemes: ɕ-kɤ-tsʰi-t-a ( tral - aor -drink- pst: tr - 1sg ) thus yields ɕ-kɯ ɕ-kɤ-tsʰi-t-a as in ( ex:CkWCkAtshita ). Tshendzin however also accepts reduplication of the first morpheme only, reduplicated with addition of -ɯ ( ɕɯ ɕ-kɤ-tsʰi-t-a).

exe

cʰa ɕkɯ ɕ-kɤ-tsʰi-t-a ʑo lu-βzi-a ŋu \\
alcohol iter tral - aor -drink- pst: tr - 1sg emph ipfv -be.drunk- 1sg be: fact \\
`Each time I go and drink alcohol I get drunk.' (elicited)
exe

Example ( ex:CtWtAkWtshAt ) illustrates a third possible pattern, with reduplication of the orientation preverb ɕ-tɤ-kɯ-tsʰɤt $ $ ɕ- tɯ tɤ-kɯ-tsʰɤt without affecting the associated motion marker.

exe

kɯki tɯrme kɯra ɕ-tɯ tɤ-kɯ-tsʰɤt ʑo nɯ pjɤ́-wɣ-sat-nɯ. \\
dem. prox person dem: pl tral - total aor - sbj: pcp -try emph dem ifr - inv -kill- pl \\
`All of these men who had went and tried [to discover the princesses' secret] were killed.' (140508 shier ge tiaowu de gongzhu-zh) 0003937#S31
exe
summary: Initial reduplication generally follows the rules of partial reduplication, but two extra patterns must be considered. The negative prefix mɯ- reduplicates as mɯ mɤ-, with vowel alternation, and when the initial syllable contains multiple morphemes, reduplication may either copy across morpheme boundaries or target only the first morpheme with added -ɯ. The passage also notes a third pattern in which only the orientation preverb is reduplicated, without affecting the associated motion marker.

text:
reduplication!protasis protasis!reduplication
There are three possibilities in Japhug to mark the verbs in the protasis of conditionals (§ sec:real.conditional ): Irrealis (§ sec:irrealis.conditional ), Interrogative ɯ- (§ sec:interrogative.W.function ) and initial reduplication. In the latter two cases, the verb is generally followed by the additive linker nɤ, as in ( ex:atCW.tWtWNu.nA ).

exe

a-tɕɯ tɯ tɯ-ŋu nɤ, pɯ-ta-sɯxɕɤt nɯ ci nɯ-ndɯn ra \\
1sg. poss -son cond 2-be: fact add aor -1 2-teach dem once imp -read be.needed: fact \\
`If you are my son, recite [the mantra] that I have taught you.' (2012 Norbzang)
0003768#S188
exe

Conditional reduplication interacts with TAME categories. For instance, reduplicated Aorist can be used to refer to hypothetical future events as in ( ex:tWtAtWtWt.nA ). Without the nɤ linker, reduplicated Aorist can be interpreted as Iterative coincidence (§ sec:iterative.coincidence ).

The scope of the protasis can go beyond the clause containing the reduplicated verb. In ( ex:tWxtsa.mWmApWpe ), the protasis contains two clauses, the first one headed by the verb mɯ mɤ-pɯ-pe with reduplicated conditional, and the second one with the verb tu-kɯ-ŋke without conditional marking.

summary:
Japhug marks conditional protases with irrealis forms, the interrogative prefix ɯ-, or initial reduplication; in the latter two cases, the verb is usually followed by the additive linker nɤ. Reduplicated conditionals interact with TAM categories: a reduplicated Aorist can express hypothetical future events, while without nɤ it may be interpreted as iterative coincidence.  

The scope of the protasis can extend beyond the clause containing the reduplicated verb, covering multiple clauses. The reduplicated conditional form pɯ pɯ-ŋu has also been grammaticalized into the topic marker pɯpɯŋunɤ, meaning ‘as far as… is concerned.’

text:
iterative coincidence!protasis protasis!iterative coincidenc
One of the meaning of initial reduplication with verbs in Aorist form is iterative coincidence. In this biclausal construction, the first clause with the reduplicated verb expresses the repetition of an event `every time $X$' (§ sec:iterative.coincidence.clause ), and the second clause (with a main verb in the Imperfective) the resulting situation, as in ( ex:tWtAGe.Zo ).

exe

[kɯki tɕʰemɤpɯ ki si ɯ-kɯ-pʰɯt tɯ-tɤ-ɣe ʑo], nɯnɯ rgɤnmɯ nɯ ɣɯ ɯ-si ɲɯ-pʰɯt, ɯ-tɯ-ci z-ɲɯ-re, \\
dem. prox girl dem. prox wood 3sg. poss - sbj: pcp -cut iter aor: up -come[II] emph dem old.woman dem gen 3sg. poss -wood ipfv -cut 3sg. poss - indef. poss -water tral - ipfv: west -fetch[III] \\
`Every time the girl came to cut firewood, she would cut firewood for the old woman and fetch water for her.' (150829 taishan zhi zhu-zh)
0006350#S26
exe

Although the semantic relationship between the two clauses is more a matter of temporal relationship rather than strict causality (for instance in example ex:tWtAGe.Zo ), this construction is clearly a subcase of the reduplicated conditional (§ sec:redp.protasis ).
summary: Initial reduplication with verbs in the Aorist can express iterative coincidence, a biclausal construction in which the first clause describes repeated events, meaning “every time X.” The second clause, usually with a main verb in the Imperfective, states the situation that results, and the relationship between the clauses is primarily temporal rather than strictly causal. This construction is treated as a subtype of the reduplicated conditional.

text:
reduplication!incremental incremental!reduplication

summary: Verb-initial reduplication with adjectival stative verbs expresses a gradual change in degree, meaning “become more and more X,” and it occurs with TAME categories that have an inchoative reading in stative contexts, especially the Imperfective, Aorist, and Inferential. The reduplicated imperfective negative mɯ-mɤ- can express gradual decrease, and reduplication can also be combined with verb repetition and the additive linker nɤ to emphasize that the increase is steady and progressive.

text:
reduplication!totalitative totalitative!reduplication relative clause!totalitative reduplication
Totalitative reduplication occurs on the main verb of relative clauses (§ sec:totalitative.relatives ), expressing universal quantification (§ sec:universal.quant ) of the relativized referent. It is attested in participial relatives (§ sec:subject.participle.other.prefixes ), finite relatives (§ sec:finite.relatives ) and also some partially lexicalized participles (§ sec:lexicalized.subject.participle ).

In the case of participial relatives, the reduplicated syllable is the first syllable of the verb other than the possessive prefix, either the subject participle prefix kɯ- ( ex:kWkWspoR.Zo ), the object participle kɤ- ( ex:kWkAsWso ) or an orientation preverb ( ex:tWtAkWrWkhArlAn ).

exe

laχtɕʰa ŋotɕu nɤ-kɤ-sɯso ʑo nɯnɯ, nɤ-mɲaʁ, nɤ-rna, nɤ-ɕna cʰo ra [kɯ kɯ-spoʁ] nɯ ɯ-ŋgɯ tɕe a-kɤ-tɯ-rke qʰe \\
thing where 2sg. poss - obj: pcp -think emph dem 2sg. poss -eye 2sg. poss -ear 2sg. poss -nose comit pl total sbj: pcp -have.a.hole dem 3sg. poss -in loc irr - pfv: east -2-put.in[III] lnk \\
`Whatever things you want (from the granary), put it in your eyes, your ears, your nose etc, all the holes in your body.' (31-deluge)
0004077#S136
exe

exe

wuma ʑo ɲɯ-pe ndɤre, [kɯ kɤ-sɯso] nɯ ɲɯ-fse \\
really emph sens -be.good lnk total obj: pcp -think dem sens -be.like \\
`It is very nice, it is like everything that [I] want.' (2011-04-smanmi)
exe

exe

tɕe ɯ-tʰɤcu prɤscʰɯ ra [tɯ tɤ-kɯ-rɯkʰɤrlɤn] kɯ nɯ-rdɤstaʁ nɯ ntsɯ s-cʰɤ-nɯ-ru-nɯ tɕe to-nɯ-ntɕʰoz-nɯ. \\
lnk 3sg. poss -downstream topo pl total aor - sbj: pcp -build.house erg 3pl. poss -stone dem always tral - ifr: downstream - auto -fetch- pl lnk ifr - auto -use- pl \\
`All people from Praskyu down there who built/repaired their houses went there and took stones to use for themselves.' (140522 Kamnyu zgo) 0004059#S188
