`[Its wing] had pus and worms grew in it, it flew so much that the base of its wing festered and had worms.' (22-qomndroN)
0003598#S47
exe

In each of the sections of this chapter on denominal prefixes, the corresponding light verb constructions are systematically indicated.

Although the two constructions are semantically very close, an important difference is that in the denominal construction, the noun cannot take external determiners like numeral and demonstratives (unlike denominal derivation in some Uto-Aztecan languages like Hopi for instance, see ). For instance, in ( ex:WrZaB.chArArJit ), the verb cʰɤ-rɤ-rɟit (from tɤ-rɟitchild, § sec:denom.intr.rA ) means `gave birth to (a) child/children', without any indication on the number of children (the unicity of the offspring in this example is deduced from the context of the story).

exe

[ɯ-rʑaβ nɯ ɯ-skʰrɯ mɯ-nɯ-kɯ-βdi] nɯ, cʰɤ-rɤ-rɟit \\
3sg. poss -wide dem 3sg. poss -body neg - aor - sbj: pcp -be.well dem ifr - denom -child \\
`His wife, who was pregnant, gave birth to a child.' (2012 Norbzang)
0003768#S95
exe

In order to specify the number of children that are born, a collocation with the verb scibe born, its causative sɯscigive birth to or the corresponding possessive construction with the verb tuexist are needed instead, as in ( ex:kWngWt.tABzu ). The same meaning cannot be expressed by combining the verb cʰɤ-rɤ-rɟit with a numeral.

exe

ɯ-rɟit kɯngɯt tɤ-tu. \\
3sg. poss -child nine aor -exist \\
`She had nine children.' (14-siblings) 0003508#S15
exe

The only cases when a denominal derivation can preserve the modifier of a noun is when the modifier is fused with the noun root and both undergo the derivation together. For instance, the nominal phrase tɕʰitɕɯn paχɕipear, which comprises the noun paχɕiapple with the placename tɕʰitɕɯnChuchen as prenominal modifier (§ ex:attributive.prenominal, § sec:determinative.n.n ) can be verbalized as nɯtɕʰitɕɯnpaχɕicollect pears with the intransitive nɯ- derivation (§ sec:denom.tr.nW ).
summary: The passage explains that many denominal derivations have meanings that are synonymous or near-synonymous with complex predicates formed with light verbs such as **βzu** ‘make’ or existential **tu** ‘exist’, and that both constructions integrate a nominal root into a predicate. It notes, however, that denominal verbs differ in that the noun cannot take external determiners like numerals or demonstratives, so number must be expressed by other constructions; only modifiers fused with the noun root can be preserved in denominal derivation.

text:
contracting verb vowel!contraction
Contracting denominal prefixes are mono- or disyllabic prefixes which first syllable is a, and undergoes vowel contraction in the contexts discussed in § sec:contraction like the passive a- (§ sec:passive ) and the reciprocal derivations (§ sec:reciprocal ).

Stative a-
denominal derivation!stative
The denominal prefix a- derives intransitive verbs. Most a- denominal verbs are stative, and either mean `be $X$' or `have the property of $X$'. The stative denominal function of a- is highly productive, and can be applied to Tibetan loanwords.

Denominal verbs in a- can express shape, as in artaʁbe forked from tɤ-rtaʁbranch. They can also refer to a more abstract property of the base noun, as in the case of acibe wet, which derives from tɯ-ciwater (on which see § sec:earth.IPN ).

Denominal verbs expressing physical defects are most often built with the a- prefix, for instance aɕkalabe lame, aʑɤwube lame and aɕquwabe blind from ɕkalalame person, ʑɤwulame person (from ཞ་བ་ʑa.bacripple) and ɕquwablind person, respectively (an exception is ɣɤmbɣobe deaf with the ɣɤ- prefix, § sec:denom.GW ).

Some denominal verbs in a- express a property shared by several entities, for instance aɕɣabe the same age (§ sec:intrinsically.n.sg.subject ) from tɯ-ɕɣatooth). The semantic extension `age' from `tooth' is also found in other Gyalrongic languages, see for instance. Such verbs can have a reduplicated stem, or suffixal syllables, like the verbs a-fsɯ fsu and a-fsu-ja both meaning `be of the same size' On the causative form of afsujabe of the same size, see § sec:sig.caus.tropative (in particular example ex:tuWGsAfsuja ). from the inalienably possessed noun ɯ-fsuof the same size (§ sec:fsu.fse, § sec:Wfsu.equative ).

Not all a- denominal verbs are stative. Dynamic intransitive verbs in a- include for instance arjuspeak (§ sec:preverb.speech ) from tɯ-rjuword, `utterance', and the verbs amqajfight (scold each other) and aɣroplay (with non-singular subjects), from tɯ-mqajscolding and tɤɣrogame The noun tɤɣrogame is however also possibly interpretable as a deverbal noun, see § sec:action.nominals., which are almost always attested with infixation of the autive nɯ- as a<nɯ>mqaj and a<nɯ>ɣro.

Compound nouns of dimension (§ sec.v.v.compounds.degree ) can derive compound verbs (§ sec:denom.compound.verbs ) meaning `of uneven/unequal $X$' or `spread along the dimension $X$' with the a- prefix, as shown in tab:denom.dimension. Among them, ajpomxtsʰɯmhave uneven thickness presents an unexplained alternation between u and o alternation: the denominal verb has o in the first syllable, while the compound noun jpumxtsʰɯmthickness and the base verb jpumbe thick have u.

The causative form of these verbs, regularly built with vowel fusion sɯ-ɤ- (§ sec:caus.sA ), means `align/put along the $X$ dimension' as in ( ex:lusAlothi ) (where the upstream-downstream dimension refers to the head-tail dimension of the body of the butterfly).

`[The butterfly] has four wings, on each side a big one and a small one. (...) When it flies, it aligns [its wings] along the `upstream-downstream' axis.' (26-qambalWla)
0003680#S45

The verbs ataʁki, alotʰi and akundi and their causative forms select the upwards, upstream (as in ex:lusAlothi ) and eastwards preverbs, respectively.

Noun-verb pairs where the verb has a- and the noun is an inalienably possessed noun selecting the tɤ- indefinite possessor prefix (for instance the verb aɕqʰecough and the inalienably possessed noun tɤ-ɕqʰecough ) can be interpreted as a- denominal derivation, but the opposite directionality (the inalienably possessed noun as a nominalized form of the a- prefixed verb) is also possible (see § sec:bare.action.nominals for a more detailed discussion). Another problematic example of a- denominal derivation is acʰɤtbe $X$ years apart (§ sec:a.non.passive.denominal ).

In some cases, semantic changes either in the verb or the noun have obscured the etymological relationship between them. For instance, it is possible that aroown is historically related to tɤ-rosurplus, leftover (§ sec:semi.transitive ), though there is no synchronic link between these two words.

A certain number of intransitive verbs in a- can be suspected of being denominal verbs whose base noun has been lost. This is particularly clear in the case of some verbs expressing shape such as aβzɯrχsɯmhave a triangular shape from a noun *βzɯrχsɯm unattested in Japhug, but attested in Tibetan as ཟུར་གསུམ་zur.gsumtriangle. Even when the nominal source is not recoverable, as in the case of artɯmbe round, the hypothesis that the a- verb comes from a lost noun (in this case, something like *rtɯm `round object, circle') can never be ruled out.

The deideophonic a- derivation (§ sec:a.nA.deidph ) is also likely to have a historical relationship with the stative a- denominal prefix.

Similative arɯ-
denominal derivation!similative similative!denominal
The prefix arɯ- derives stative verbs meaning `be $X$-like, be similar to $X$' from a nominal base. tab:arW.denom presents a few representative examples of this prefix. Although these verbs (with the exception of arɯldʑaŋkɯbe green) are relatively rare in the corpus, this derivation is extremely productive and can be applied to Tibetan loanwords, for instance ɕoʁɕoʁpaper, ldʑaŋkɯgreen and mɯntoʁflower (from ཤོག་ཤོག་ɕog.ɕogpaper, ལྗང་གུ་ldʑaŋ.gugreen and མེ་ཏོག་me.togflower, respectively. It is even found on Chinese loanwords such as 喇叭 lǎbahorn.

Inalienably possessed nouns such as tɤ-tɕɯson, `boy' are denominalized together with their indefinite possessor prefix (§ sec:kinship ).

The arɯ- derivation can take not only noun roots, but also noun phrases as input. For instance, the phrase qro-mke ɯ-mdoʁ (pigeon-neck 3sg. poss -colour) `purple, colour of the pigeon's neck' can be denominalized as arɯqromkemdoʁbe purple.

With colour nouns, including those borrowed from Tibetan like ldʑaŋkɯgreen and ʁmɤrsmɯɣdark red (§ sec:tibetan.colours ) and others like qro-mke ɯ-mdoʁ `purple', the denominal verbs in arɯ- simply mean `be $X$, have the colour $X$', as in ( ex:arWldZaNkW ).

exe
summary:
The prefix **a-** derives intransitive denominal verbs, most often stative ones meaning ‘be X’ or ‘have the property of X,’ and it is highly productive, including with Tibetan loanwords. These verbs can also express shapes, abstract properties, defects, shared properties, and in some cases dynamic meanings; some are historically linked to lost nouns or have an unclear etymology, and a related deideophonic derivation may be historically connected to this prefix.  

The prefix **arɯ-** derives stative verbs meaning ‘be X-like’ or ‘be similar to X’ from nominal bases, and this derivation is also highly productive, including with Tibetan and Chinese loanwords. It can apply to noun phrases as well as nouns, and with colour terms it simply means ‘be X’ or ‘have the colour X.’

Denominal verbs in arɯ- are often used in similative constructions with degree nominals, either as nominal predicates as in ( ex:WtArWmWntoR ) (§ sec:degree.nominal.predicates ) or in the degree construction ( ex:YArWtAjpa ) (§ sec:degree.nominal.construction ). Note that the connotation of these similative verbs can be culture-specific: although arɯmɯntoʁbe like a flower can be understood as `be as beautiful as a flower', its most natural interpretation is surprisingly `worthless' (because flowers are viewed as not lasting long, and prone to withering).

Proprietive arɤ-
denominal derivation!proprietive proprietive!denominal
The arɤ- denominal prefix has a proprietive meaning, and is generally correlated with partial reduplication of the nominal stem as in arɤrqʰɯrqʰioʁbe grooved ( ex:kArArqhWrqhioR ) from tɤ-rqʰioʁgroove.

exe

ɯ-ru nɯra tɤ-kɯ-ɤrɤ-rqʰɯ rqʰioʁ kɯ-fse ci ŋu qʰe, \\
3sg. poss -stalk dem: pl aor - sbj: pcp - denom -groove sbj: pcp -be.like indef be: fact lnk \\
`Its stalk is like it has had many groovings on it.' (14-sWNgWJu) 0003506#S41
exe

The arɤ- prefix can also be used to derive verbs from counted nouns as for instance arɤɕɯɕrɤzbe striped from tɯ-ɕrɤzone stripe. The verb arɤkʰɯmkʰɤlbe clustered in patches, `not homogeneously distributed' from tɯ-kʰɤlone place has the very rare partial reduplication pattern in -ɯm ( arɤ-kʰɯm kʰɤl, § sec.distributed.action.oR ).

Non-reduplicated arɤ- denominal verbs are also found, for instance arɤtsʰibe cooked like rice gruel (from tɯtsʰirice gruel, a lexicalized nominalization from tsʰidrink) and arɤrɤɣhappen at the predicted time from ɯ-rɤɣpredicted time (on which see § sec:relator.temporal ).

exe

aʑo a-ʑɯβ ɲɤ-k-ɤrɤ-rɤɣ-ci \\
1sg 1sg. poss -sleep ifr - peg - denom -predicted.time- peg \\
`I feel sleepy at the expected time.' (elicited, can be said when one feels sleepy at the same hour in the afternoon when one went to sleep the previous days)
exe

Like other compound denominal prefixes (§ sec:denom.aGW.caus ), the arɤ- prefix loses its a- element when subjected to causative derivation. For instance, arɤtsʰibe cooked like rice gruel has the causative form zrɤtsʰicook like rice gruel (§ sec:sigm.caus.a.z ).

The arɤ- prefix should not be confused with the reciprocal from transitive verbs in rɤ-. For instance arɤzdɯzdacall each other (before departure) does not directly come from the noun tɯ-zdacompanion, but is rather the reduplicated reciprocal (§ sec:redp.reciprocal ) of the denominal verb rɤzdacall before departure derived from this noun.

Proprietive aɣɯ-
denominal derivation!proprietive proprietive!denominal
The prefix aɣɯ- derives proprietive stative verbs meaning `have a lot of $X$' or `produce a lot of $X$'. For instance, Tshendzin provided the definition in ( ex:YAGWmdzu.def ) for the proprietive denominal aɣɯ-mdzu from tɤ-mdzuthorn.

exe

ɲɯ-ɤɣɯ-mdzu, ɯ-taʁ tɤ-mdzu ɲɯ-dɤn kɤ-ti ɲɯ-ŋu. \\
sens - denom: prop -thorn 3sg. poss -on indef. poss -thorn sens -be.many obj: pcp -say sens -be \\
`[The word] ɲɯ-ɤɣɯ-mdzu means `there are a lot of thorns on it'.' (elicited)
exe

When the base noun is inalienably possessed (§ sec:inalienably.possessed ) or when it is a counted noun (§ sec:counted.nouns ), the denominal prefix is directly attached to the root, and the indefinite possessor prefixes tɯ, tɤ, ta- or the numeral prefixes are removed, as shown in the examples in tab:aGW.denom. The aɣɯ- prefix is invariable, without an allomorph such as $ $ aɣɤ- as could have been expected (§ sec:indef.genr.poss ) when the base noun selects the indefinite possessor prefix tɤ-.

This prefix is very productive, and occurs on nominal bases borrowed from Tibetan (such as rŋɯlsilver, ɯ-mdoʁcolour, tɯɣpoison and smɤnmedicine (respectively from དངུལ་dŋulsilver, མདོག་mdogcolour, དུག་dugpoison and སྨན་smanmedicine) and even Chinese ( tɯ-ʂwaŋa pair from 双 shuāngpair).

Another possible meaning of the aɣɯ- prefix is `be the same $X$', as in the case of aɣɯmdoʁbe the same colour from ɯ-mdoʁcolour. These types of verbs have non-singular intransitive subjects, as in ( ex:aGWmdoR.arNi ) with a comitative phrase (§ sec:comitative ). Concerning the absence of dual indexation on the verbs in ( ex:aGWmdoR.arNi ), see § sec:optional.indexation.

exe

ɯ-ru cʰo ɯ-fkaβ ra aɣɯmdoʁ ʑo arŋi. \\
3sg. poss -stalk comit 3sg. poss -cover pl denom -colour: fact emph be.green: fact \\
`Its stalk and its cap are the same green colour.' (of a species of mushroom) (22-BlamajmAG)

A few aɣɯ- denominal verbs, such as aɣɯtɯɣbe poisonous from tɯɣpoison, have a more abstract proprietive function (`have the property of $X$') like that of the sɤ- prefix (note the synonym sɤndɤɣbe poisonous, § sec:denom.sA.proprietive ). Other semantic values of the aɣɯ- prefix are discussed in § sec:denom.aGW.lexicalized.

The aɣɯ- denominal prefix has cognates in other Gyalrong languages, for example ɐwə- in Tshobdun.

reduplication!proprietive
Emphatic reduplication (§ sec:emph.redp ) is possible as an option on denominal verbs, but some verbs in aɣɯ- occur with obligatory reduplication of the nominal root, for instance aɣɯjɯjaʁhave a lot of arms and aɣɯmɯmihave a lot of legs ( ex:YAGWjWJaR ). Note that the alternative form aɣɯjaʁ without reduplication is also attested, but with a completely different meaning (§ sec:denom.aGW.lexicalized ).

Only a few causative verbs derived from aɣɯ- denominal verbs are attested. Instead of expected vowel fusion ($ $ sɯ-ɤɣɯ- sɤɣɯ, see § sec:caus.sA ), the a- element is dropped and replaced by the z- allomorph of the sigmatic causative (§ sec:sigm.caus.a.z ). For instance, the stative verb aɣɯŋgɯŋgɯhave a lot of layers (from ɯ-ŋgɯinside, with reduplication, § sec:denom.aGW.redp ) has the causative form zɣɯŋgɯŋgɯput on a lot of layers as in ( ex:pjAzGWNgWNgW ).

The semantics of the aɣɯ- derivation is not always trivially predictable.

Some of the lexicalized meanings are relatable to one of the basic functions of this prefix. For instance, aɣɯʂwaŋbe a match (to each other) ( ex:mWpjAkAGWsxWaNci ) from tɯ-ʂwaŋa pair presumably derives from an earlier `have the property of being a pair'.

Other denominal verbs have meanings that are completely unpredictable. For example, the denominal verb aɣɯjaʁ from tɯ-jaʁhand, arm, rather than meaning `have arms' as expected (see however § sec:denom.aGW.redp ), either occurs in the sense of `fidget, touch other peoples' things (like a thief)' or `do things (with one's hands) quickly'. The metaphorical extensions on which the unpredictable meanings of aɣɯ- are sometimes shared with other denominal derivations. For instance, aɣɯrpaʁgo along well (with non-singular subject) from tɯ-rpaʁshoulder presents the same semantic derivation as the transitive denominal verb nɤrpaʁgo along well with (from `carry on the shoulder', § sec:denom.nW ).

Some lexicalized aɣɯ- denominal verbs additionally present unusual argument structure. Unlike other aɣɯ- verbs which are plain intransitives, aɣɯrɯzinherit from (either from ɯ-rɯzspecies, borrowed from རིགསrigsrace, or from རུསrusbone, lineage) is a semi-transitive verb (§ sec:semi.transitive ), taking as semi-object the person or group of people one inherits a trait from as in ( ex:tWmu.ra.anWkAGWrWz ).

text:
comitative adverb
The aɣɯ- denominal derivation has served as the basis for the development of a separatee morphological category: denominal comitative adverbs (, § sec:comitative.adverb ).

Comitative adverbs are built by combining the prefix kɤɣɯ- (or kɤ́, a borrowing from Tshobdun, § sec:comitative.adverb ) to the partially reduplicated stem of the base noun, as in kɤɣɯ-rtɯ rtaʁ `together with its branches' from tɤ-rtaʁbranch or kɤɣɯ-rɟɯ rɟit `together with his/her/its children' from tɤ-rɟitchild. These adverbs are formally homophonous with the kɯ- subject participles (§ sec:subject.participles ) or stative infinitives (§ sec:infinitives.participles ) of the aɣɯ- denominal verbs with emphatic reduplication (§ sec:denom.aGW.redp ).
comitative adverb
For example, the surface form kɤɣɯrtɯrtaʁ can be parsed either as a comitative adverb kɤɣɯ-rtɯ rtaʁ `together with its branches' or as the participle kɯ-ɤɣɯ-rtɯ rtaʁ `the one which has many branches' as in ( ex:kAGWrtWrtaR ).

comitative adverb reanalysis
The comitative adverbs result from the reanalysis of a non-finite form of proprietive aɣɯ- denominal verb, possibly a subject participle or an infinitive in converbial function (§ sec:inf.converb ), with a trivial semantic change from proprietive `have many $X$' to comitative `together with $X$' (on the semantic proximity of the two categories, see for instance ).

Collective andʑi-
denominal derivation!collective collective!denominal
The andʑi- collective denominal prefix is attested in only one example:

This prefix is historically related to the andʑɯ- reciprocal (§ sec:andZW.reciprocal ), and the social collective kɤndʑi- prefix (§ sec:social.collective ) derives from the combination of the denominal andʑi- with the kɯ- subject participle prefix (§ sec:subject.participles ). summary:
The passage explains that denominal comitative adverbs developed from an aɣɯ- denominal derivation and are formed with the prefix kɤɣɯ- (or borrowed kɤ́) plus a partially reduplicated noun stem, meaning roughly “together with X.” These forms are homophonous with certain participles or stative infinitives, and the same surface forms can therefore be analyzed either as comitative adverbs or as proprietary participles, with the comitative reading seen as a reanalysis from a non-finite verb form.

It also notes a rare collective denominal prefix andʑi-, attested in only one example meaning “neighbours” or “one next to the other,” historically related to the reciprocal andʑɯ-. The social collective kɤndʑi- is derived from this prefix plus the kɯ- participle prefix, and the exact historical formation of the prefix remains unclear

text:
Proprietive sɤ-
denominal derivation!proprietive proprietive!denominal
Proprietive verbs in sɤ- are derived from nouns in tɤ, either from inalienably possessed nouns selecting the indefinite possessor prefix tɤ- (§ sec:inalienably.possessed ) or from nouns with a frozen tɤ- prefix. These stative verbs are almost always paired with corresponding dynamic verbs in nɤ- (more rarely nɯ, § sec:denom.nW.pairing ). As shown by tab:sA.denom.proprietive, the base nouns can either be entities ( tɤ-ndɤɣpoison) or actions ( tɤ-relaugh (n)). The proprietive denominal verbs, like sɤ- proprietive verbs (§ sec:proprietive ), take as intransitive subject the stimulus of the action (perceptible by or affecting other entities). They have a meaning very close to that of the aɣɯ- proprietive denominal verbs (§ sec:denom.aGW ), in particular aɣɯtɯɣbe poisonous from tɯɣpoison, which has the same meaning as sɤndɤɣbe poisonous.

The corresponding nɯ-/nɤ- verbs can be either intransitive, transitive or labile (§ sec:lability.categories ). Their subject corresponds to the experiencer of the perception/feeling caused by the stimulus. When used transitively, these verbs select the stimulus as object, like tropative verbs (§ sec:tropative ): the intransitive subject of sɤrebe ridiculous and sɤmtsʰɤrbe strange is the same entity as the object of nɤre `laugh at' and nɤmtsʰɤrfind strange.

The presence of the loanword -mtsʰɤr from མཚར་mtsʰarwondrous, strange among the verbs in tab:sA.denom.proprietive shows that both denominal derivations are productive.

The historical relationship between denominal sɤ- and nɤ- prefixes on the one hand, and proprietive and tropative prefixes on the other hand, is explored in § sec:sA.history.

Proprietive denominal verbs in sɤ- do not have tropative forms, and instead form the corresponding nɤ- denominal verb instead. For instance sɤŋaβbe unpleasant, `be embarrassing' ( ex:sANAB ) lacks a tropative $ $ nɤ-sɤŋaβ, and instead requires the corresponding transitive denominal tropative nɤŋaβconsider to be unpleasant, `be embarrassed by/to' ( ex:kWnANAB ).

Causative/instrumental sV-
denominal derivation!instrumental instrumental!denominal
The sigmatic prefix sɯ(ɣ)- / sɤ- has a causative `cause to be/have $X$' or instrumental `use $X$' denominal function. As illustrated in tab:sW.denom, most of the denominal verbs derived with this prefix are morphologically transitive, the only exceptions being sɯʁejlube left-handed (`use the left hand') and sɯndzɯpesit without crossing legs.

The sɯ(ɣ)- / sɤ- allomorphy of this denominal prefix has similarities with that of the sigmatic causative (§ sec:sig.caus.allomorphs ). The allomorph sɤ- is selected when the base noun is an inalienably possessed noun selecting the tɤ- indefinite possessor prefix (such as tɤ-kʰɯsmoke) or with frozen tɤ- prefix (such as tɤɕɤtcomb), sɯɣ-/sɯx- occurs with monosyllabic nominal roots without cluster and uvular or velar onsets such as tsʰaʁsieve (a context similar to that of the sɯɣ- allomorph of the sigmatic causative, § sec:caus.sWG ), and sɯ- is found in all other contexts, including inalienably possessed nouns selecting the tɯ- indefinite prefix ( tɯ-jaʁndzufinger) and/or non-inalienably possessed nouns with initial clusters.

Denominal verbs in sɯ(ɣ)- / sɤ- do not correspond to a single light verb construction. In the case of sɯndzɯpesit without crossing legs, the denominal derivation has a meaning similar to that of the base noun ndzɯpe `sitting position of women on the ground, without crossing legs' in collocations with the light verb βzumake (§ sec:Bzu.lv ) as in ( ex:ndzWpe.YWwGBzu ).

The sɤ- denominal derivation is productive, as shown by the presence of several words of Tibetan origin in tab:sW.denom, including tɤɕɤtcomb, fsaŋfumigation, tsʰaʁsieve, tsʰwidye and ftɕakamethod from ཤད་ɕadcomb, བསང་bsaŋfumigation, ཚགས་tsʰagssieve, ཚོས་tsʰosdye and བཅའ་ཀ་bca.katool, respectively.

Unlike other denominal prefixes such as nɯ- / nɤ, which can be paired with other prefixes (§ sec:denom.nW.pairing ), verbs derived by the sɯ(ɣ)- / sɤ- generally don't appear in sets. The groups of denominal verbs including a transitive sV- prefix are all different from each other. There is one case of sɤ- / ɣɤ- / nɤ- contrast between sɤkʰɯ `smoke' (by directing smoke towards), `burn into smoke' (see ex:tAkhW.tusWxCenW above) and the intransitive verbs ɣɤkʰɯbe smoky with the ɣɤ- prefix (example ex:kha.YWGAkhWnW, § sec:denom.GW ) and nɤkʰɯbe smoked (§ sec:denom.intr.nW ). Another group of denominal verbs comprising sɤftɕakaprepare with a contrast between sɤ, rɯ- and nɯ- is discussed in § sec:denom.rA.pairing.

The verb sɤrmigive a name (§ sec:semi.transitive.causative ) could be analyzed as an irregular causative of rmibe called (§ sec:sig.caus.irregular.other ), but the vocalism of the prefix is better accounted for by analyzing it instead as a denominal verb from the noun tɤ-rminame, which may itself originates from the base verb rmibe called.

The historical relationship between the sigmatic causative and the denominal sɯ- prefix is explored in more detail in § sec:sW.caus.history. Another related derivation is that of the sɤ- transitive deideophonic verbs (§ sec:GA.sA.deidph ).
summary: The passage illustrates how several denominal verbs in the language correspond semantically either to noun-plus-verb collocations or to specialized causative/instrumental meanings, while some have only partial or no equivalent light-verb construction. It also notes that the sɯ(ɣ)- / sɤ- denominal derivation is productive, especially with Tibetan loanwords, but that these verbs usually do not form systematic prefix pairs like some other denominal classes. A few verbs, such as sɤftɕaka `prepare' and sɤrmi `give a name', are discussed as cases where the denominal analysis is preferred over alternative historical derivations.

text: The rɯ-/rɤ- prefix is among the most productive denominal prefixes in Japhug, and has a wide range of meanings. Although not used in deideophonic derivations, it is used to borrow verbs and adjectives from Chinese (§ sec:zh.loanverbs ).
summary: The rɯ-/rɤ- prefix is one of the most productive denominal prefixes in Japhug and has a broad range of meanings. While it is not used in deideophonic derivations, it is used to borrow verbs and adjectives from Chinese.

text:
The rɯ-/rɤ- denominal prefix is mainly used to derive intransitive verbs, of which tab:denom.rA.intr provides a representative sample.

With the exception of adjectives from Chinese (§ sec:zh.loanverbs ), denominal verbs in rɯ-/rɤ- are dynamic, and have three main meanings.

First, they can mean `produce/grow/get $X$' when the base noun corresponds to a part of the referent designated by the subject of the denominal verb (for instance rɤjwaʁgrow leaves from tɤ-jwaʁleaf), or an excrescence/offspring growing out of it. The intransitive subjects of such verbs are typically plants, inanimate objects (including body parts), but also humans or animals with meanings such as `give birth to $X$' (for instance rɤrɟithave a child from tɤ-rɟitchild).

These denominal verbs have meanings similar to collocations involving several light verbs. For instance, rɤjwaʁgrow leaves and rɤmatgrow fruits are synonymous with complex predicates comprising their base nouns tɤ-jwaʁleaf and ɯ-matfruit combined with the light verbs lɤtrelease and βzumake, as shown in ( ex:YWlAt.YWBze ). Additional examples of denominal verbs belonging to this category that are synonymous with complex predicates in βzumake are discussed in § sec:denominal.vs.light.verb.

exe

nɯ [ɯ-jwaʁ ɲɯ-lɤt] tɕendɤre [ɯ-mat ɲɯ-βze] \\
dem 3sg. poss -leaf ipfv -release lnk 3sg. poss -fruit ipfv -make[III] \\
`[The Zanthoxyllum] makes leaves and grows fruits.' (07-tCGom)
0003434#S21
exe

Second, a related meaning of the rɯ-/rɤ- denominal prefix is `build $X$', when the product of the action results from a volitional action and is separate from the body of the agent, encoded as intransitive subject. Denominal verbs of this type, such as rɤloʁmake a nest and rɤkʰabuild a house, systematically correspond to complex predicates with the verb βzumake, such as kʰa+βzu `build a house' and tɤ-loʁ+βzu `make a nest'. These constructions select human or animal subjects.

Third, when the base noun refers to an activity rather than an object, the meaning of the rɯ-/rɤ- denominal verb is `do $X$, perform a $X$'. There are two types of complex predicates corresponding to this subtype of denominal verbs.

On the one hand, as in the previous subtypes, verbs such as rɯkʰrambatell lies (from kʰrambalie) or rɤkrɤzhave a discussion (from tɯkrɤzdiscussion), rɯstɯnmɯmarry (from stɯnmɯmarriage) Tibetan loanwords are common in this category; the three base nouns in the examples given here come from
ཁྲམ་པ་kʰram.baliar, གྲོས་grosdiscussion and སྟོན་མོ་ston.mobanquet, respectively. are synonymous with constructions in βzumake, kʰramba+βzu and tɯkrɤz+βzu, respectively.

On the other hand, verbs such as rɯskɤrwado circumambulations (from skɤrwacircumambulation) and rɯjɤɣɤtgo to the toilet (from jɤɣɤtterrace, `toilet') instead correspond to collocations with the motion verb ɕego (§ sec:motion.light.verbs ).

Third, in a few cases such as rɯɟuliplay the flute (from ɟuliflute), the meaning of the denominal derivation is `use $X$', and the corresponding complex predicate selects the light verb lɤtrelease ( ɟuli+lɤt `play the flute', see ex:Juli.chAlAt, § sec:preverb.speech ).

Fourth, rɯ-/rɤ- denominal verbs from nouns of profession can have the meaning `become $X$', for instance in the case of rɤχpɯnbecome a monk from χpɯnmonk. The corresponding complex predicate involves the transitive verb ndotake (§ sec:ndo.lv ). Most nouns of this type however take the intransitive denominal nɯ- to derive a verb with this meaning (§ sec:denom.intr.nW ).

In addition to nouns, the rɯ-/rɤ- denominal derivations also takes as input lexicalized nominalized verb forms. For example, the lexicalized participles kɯŋuright thing and kɯmaʁbad thing (from the subject participles kɯ-ŋuthe one that is and kɯ-maʁthe one that is not, § sec:lexicalized.subject.participle ) take the rɯ- denominal prefix to form the verbs rɯkɯŋudo the right thing, `take good care of one's family' and rɯkɯmaʁdo bad things, respectively. The corresponding complex predicate selects the verb nɤmado, see ex:kWNu.mAtWnAme in § sec:lexicalized.subject.participle. Another example is rɯtɯsqaeat wheat gruel, discussed in more details in § sec:denominalization.action.nominal and § sec:denominal.prefixes.morph.

The rɯ-/rɤ- prefix also has a deadverbial function, as in the case of rɯʁlɤwɯrhappen suddenly which comes from the adverb ʁlɤwɯrsuddenly (itself borrowed from གློ་བུར་glo.bursudden). This verb expresses an action taking place spontaneously as in ( ex:rWRlAwWr ), as opposed to that expressed by the corresponding nɯ- verb nɯʁlɤwɯrdo suddenly (§ sec:denom.intr.nW ).

exe

kʰɤrɯm nɯnɯ, tɯ-mtɕʰi ɯ-taʁ ʑmbɤr ɲɯ-kɯ-ɬoʁ ŋu. tɕe wuma ʑo rɯʁlɤwɯr \\
mouth.ulcer dem indef. poss -mouth 3sg. poss -on ulcer ipfv - sbj: pcp -come.out be: fact lnk really emph denom -suddenly \\
`[The disease called] kʰɤrɯm is an ulcer which appears on the mouth. It happens very suddenly.' (25-khArWm) 0003644#S2
exe
summary:
The rɯ-/rɤ- denominal prefix mainly derives intransitive, dynamic verbs with several semantic patterns. It can mean ‘produce/grow/get X’ when the noun names a part or offspring of the subject, ‘build X’ for volitional making of separate products, and ‘do X’ when based on activity nouns; it also has smaller senses such as ‘use X,’ ‘become X,’ and a deadverbial use meaning ‘happen suddenly.’  

Many of these verbs correspond to complex predicates with light verbs such as βzu ‘make,’ lɤt ‘release,’ ɕe ‘go,’ or ndo ‘take,’ and some nouns of profession or lexicalized nominalized forms can also serve as bases for this derivation.

text:
Transitive denominal verbs in rɤ- are also attested, but are considerably rarer. tab:denom.rA.tr presents most attested examples.

Most transitive denominal verbs in rɤ- take counted nouns (§ sec:counted.nouns ) as input. Three different meanings can be distinguished. First, rɤ- denominal verbs from counted noun expressing units of lengths (see tab:length.cn, § sec:measures ) mean `measure by $X$', as in the case of rɤtɣameasure by handspan ( ex:chWwGrAtGa ).

exe

tʰɤstɯɣ kɯ-ra nɯ cʰɯ́-wɣ-rɤ-tɣa \\
how.much sbj: pcp -be.needed dem ipfv: downstream - denom -handspan \\
`One measures how long [the clothes have to be weaved] by handspan.' (vid-20140429092115)
exe

Second, when the base noun has the meaning `(one) section', the rɤ- denominal verb derived from it means `cut/turn into $X$', like corresponding complex predicates with either lɤtrelease, βzumake or the causative sɯxɕesend, `cause to go'. Example ( ex:pjArwGrzWrzWG ) illustrates the parallel uses of the denominal verb rɤrzɯɣcut into sections and the complex predicate X-rzɯɣ+lɤt. Emphatic reduplication on the verb pjɤ́-wɣ-rɤ-rzɯ rzɯɣ contributes to express the fact that the patient is cut into more than two sections.

exe

pjɤ́-wɣ-rɤ-rzɯ rzɯɣ tɕe kɯβde-rzɯɣ ʑo tó-wɣ-lɤt, pjɤ́-wɣ-sat. \\
ipfv - inv - denom - emph section lnk four-section emph ifr - inv -release ifr - inv -kill \\
`[The thief] killed him by cutting him into four pieces.' (140512 alibaba-zh)
0003965#S109
exe

Third, in the case of the counted noun tɯ-spraone handful which refers to the volume contained in a handful, the denominal verb means `take a handful of', `hold in one hand' as in ( ex:kurAspra ).

exe

ɯ-jɯ, ɯ-sɤ-ndo [tɯ-jaʁ kɯ kú-wɣ-rɤ-spra kɯ-kʰɯ] jamar mɤɕtʂa cʰɯ́-wɣ-βʑoʁ \\
3sg. poss -handle 3sg. poss - obl: pcp -take genr. poss -hand erg ipfv - inv - denom -handful sbj: pcp -be.possible about until ipfv - inv -peel/sharpen \\
`One sharpens its handle until it can be held in one's hand.' (13-tAsAsqAri)
0003496#S21
exe

There are two transitive denominal verbs in rɤ- that are not derived from counted nouns: rɤpʰɯgive a price for from the inalienably possessed noun ɯ-pʰɯprice and rɤɴqrado in an incomplete way from the property noun ɯ-ɴqrabroken one (§ sec:property.nouns ). The former has the lexicalized reflexive ʑɣɤrɤpʰɯact according to one's ability The meaning of this verb is close to that of the Chinese expression 量力而行 liànglìérxíngact according to one's ability. (probably through an intermediate meaning such as `(correctly) evaluate one's price', § sec:lexicalized.refl ).
summary:
Transitive denominal verbs in **rɤ-** are attested but relatively rare, and most are derived from counted nouns. Depending on the noun, they can mean ‘measure by X’ for units of length, ‘cut/turn into X’ for section nouns, or ‘take a handful of/hold in one hand’ for the noun meaning ‘one handful.’  

Two transitive **rɤ-** verbs are not based on counted nouns: **rɤpʰɯ** ‘give a price for’ and **rɤɴqrɤ** ‘do in an incomplete way.’ The former also has a lexicalized reflexive meaning ‘act according to one’s ability.’

text:
denominal derivation!pairing
Intransitive denominal verbs with the rɯ-/rɤ- denominal prefix (§ sec:denom.intr.rA ) are often paired with denominal verbs in nɯ-/nɤ-. Several categories of rV-/nV- pairs have to be distinguished.

There are pairs of intransitive verbs, such as rɯqajɯget worms and nɯqajɯlook for worms from qajɯworm, where the rV- verb means `produce/grow/get $X$' (§ sec:denom.intr.rA ), while the nV- verb rather has the meaning `look for/search/collect $X$' (§ sec:denom.intr.nW ).

However, in most cases the rV- verb is intransitive and the nV- one is transitive. For instance, rɤmawork ( ex:turAmandZi ) has intransitive morphology (no stem II alternation), no overt object and its subject is in absolutive form, while its counterpart nɤmado (a job) has stem III alternation and its subject is marked in the ergative ( ex:YWnAme and ex:Wma.tunAme ) (§ sec:transitivity.morphology ). The intransitive subject of the rV- denominal verb and the transitive subject of the nV- encode the same referent.

exe

nɯtɕu a-wi cʰo a-mu ni tu-rɤ-ma-ndʑi, \\
dem: loc 1sg. poss -grandmother comit 1sg. poss -mother du ipfv - denom: tr -work- du \\
`My grandmother and my mother were working there.' (2010-09)
exe

The additional object argument of the nV- verb which can be a noun phrase as in ( ex:YWnAme ), with a figura etymologica ɯ-ma+nɤma `do $X$'s work' in ( ex:Wma.tunAme ).

exe

kʰa nɯra ɲɯ-nɤ-me. \\
house dem: pl sens - denom: tr -work[III] \\
`[Her daughter] does the housework.' (14-siblings) 0003508#S60
exe

exe

ɯʑo kɯ rɟɤlpu ɯ-ma tu-nɤ-me \\
3sg erg king 3sg. poss -work ipfv - denom: tr -work[III] \\
`He did the work of a king.' (2003 qachGa) 0003372#S196
exe

In the case of other verbs pairs such as rɤkrɤzhave a discussion and nɯkrɤzdiscuss (something), the object of the nV- verb is an infinitive complement clause, as in ( ex:tonWkrAzndZi ). In some cases the transitive verb nɯkrɤz has the additional meaning `discuss and decide that $X$'.

exe

kʰu cʰondɤre mbro ni to-rɤ-krɤz-ndʑi. [...] [tɯ-rɟit kɤ́-wɣ-nɯskʰrɯ tɕe,
ɯ-pɯ nɯ tɕʰi jamar tɕe tu-kɤ-sci nɯ], to-nɯ-krɤz-ndʑi. \\
tiger comit horse du ifr - denom: intr -discussion- du
genr. poss -offspring aor - inv -be.pregnant.from lnk 3sg. poss -child dem what about lnk ipfv - inf -be.born dem ifr - denom: tr -discussion- du \\
`The tigress and the mare had a discussion, they discussed how long it would take for the child to be born after one gets pregnant.' (20-tArka) 0003566#S33
exe

The relationship between the rV- and the nV- verbs is functionally similar to a base verb and its applicative counterpart, or to an antipassive verb and its corresponding base verb (§ sec:antipassive.vs.denominal.pairs, § sec:denom.nW.pairing ). The high degree of productivity of this type of denominal pair is shown by the presence not only of Tibetan loanwords among the examples, but also of loanwords from Chinese such as rɯkʰɤjxwihave a meeting and nɯkʰɤjxwimeet about (from 开会 kāihuìhave a meeting, § sec:zh.loanverbs ).

The semantics of the verbs rɯftɕakado preparation and nɯftɕakaprepare, like that of sɤftɕakaprepare (§ sec:denom.sW.caus.instr ), derives from the collocation ftɕaka+βzu `prepare $X$, prepare to $X$' (the other meanings of this collocation are discussed in, § sec:inf.complementation
and § sec:infinitives.other.prefixes ) rather than from the noun ftɕakamethod itself. Both nɯftɕaka and ftɕaka+βzu can occur with infinitival complement clauses ( ex:kuwGnWftCaka ) or nouns ( ex:ftɕaka.tABze in § sec:denom.sW.caus.instr ) as objects. The intransitive rɯftɕaka occurs as the functional antipassive counterpart of both nɯftɕaka and sɤftɕaka.

exe

li kɤ-tɤβ kú-wɣ-nɯ-ftɕaka ra [...] tɤ-tɕɯ ra kɯ tɕendɤre kɤ-tɤβ ftɕaka tú-wɣ-βzu tɕe, \\
again inf -thresh ipfv - inv - denom -manner be.needed: fact indef. poss -boy pl erg lnk inf -thresh manner ipfv - inv -make lnk \\
`(After...), one has to prepare the threshing, the men prepare to thresh [the crops].' (2010-10)
exe
summary:
The passage describes several productive pairs of denominal verbs with rV- and nV- prefixes. In some pairs both verbs are intransitive, with rV meaning ‘produce/grow/get X’ and nV meaning ‘look for/search/collect X,’ but more often the rV-verb is intransitive while the nV-verb is transitive and takes an object or complement, with the same core referent expressed by the subject of rV and the subject of nV.  

These pairs often resemble a base verb and applicative counterpart or an antipassive and base verb, and they are highly productive, including borrowings from Tibetan and Chinese. In some cases, the meanings of the verbs are better explained by an underlying collocation than by the noun itself, and the intransitive rV form functions as the antipassive counterpart of both transitive forms.

text: The ɣɤ- denominal prefix (and its rarer variant ɣɯ- has a considerable variety of meanings, and can be used to derive both transitive and intransitive verbs. It is commonly paired with nɯ-/nɤ- (§ sec:denom.GA.pairing ). In addition, it is among the denominal prefixes used to borrow adjectives from Chinese (§ sec:zh.loanverbs ) and to build incorporating verbs (§ sec:incorporation ).
summary: The ɣɤ- denominal prefix, along with the rarer ɣɯ- variant, has a wide range of meanings and can derive both transitive and intransitive verbs. It is often paired with nɯ-/nɤ- and is also used in borrowing adjectives from Chinese and in forming incorporating verbs.

text:
The ɣɤ- prefix can derive several types of intransitive verbs, of which tab:denom.GA.intr lists a representative sample.

Some ɣɤ- denominal verbs are stative proprietive, like those in aɣɯ- (§ sec:denom.aGW ), such as ɣɤrcoʁbe muddy from tɤrcoʁmud. The base nouns can be inalienably possessed nouns, nouns with a frozen tɤ- prefix, alienably possessed nouns (such as rdɯldust) and also property nouns (such as ɯ-jluuncooked, § tab:property.nouns ). The only example of a Tibetan loanword among these nouns is rdɯldust (from རྡུལ་rduldust). Unlike aɣɯ, the ɣɤ- prefix can derive verbs from abstract nouns, such as ɣɤndʐobe cold from tɤndʐo `cold weather'.

Different nouns belonging to the same semantic categories do not necessarily select the same denominal prefix. For instance, the inalienably possessed noun ɯ-dɯχɯnfragrance is the base for the denominal verb aɣɯdɯχɯnbe fragrant with the aɣɯ- prefix, while the noun tɤ-dismell (from which ɯ-dɯχɯnfragrance is derived) takes the ɣɤ- denominal prefix ( ɣɤdihave a smell, `stink'). Similarly, while most denominal verbs expressing physical defects are built with the a- prefix (§ sec:denom.a ), the verb ɣɤmbɣobe deaf (from tɤmbɣodeaf person) has the ɣɤ- prefix.

The meaning of the ɣɤ- prefix is slightly different from that of aɣɯ-. Some nouns can take both prefixes, such as tɤ-mdzuthorn, which is the base for two denominal verbs: aɣɯmdzuhave a lot of thorns (see the Japhug definition of this verb in ex:YAGWmdzu.def, § sec:denom.aGW ) and ɣɤmdzuhave thorns.

The aɣɯ- denominal prefix indicates the presence of an important quantity of the substance or entity referred to by the base noun (`have a lot of $X$' or `produce a lot of $X$'), while ɣɤ- prefix rather can be simply glossed as `have $X$', without specification of quantity, as shown by the definition in ( ex:YWGAmdzu.def ).

exe

ɲɯ-ɣɤ-mdzu tɕe tɤ-mdzu ɣɤʑu kɤ-ti ŋu ma kɯ-dɤn mɤ-kɯ-dɤn nɯra maʁ\\
sens - denom: prop -thorn lnk indef. poss -thorn exist: sens obj: pcp -say be: fact lnk sbj: pcp -be.a.lot neg - sbj: pcp -be.a.lot dem: pl not.be: fact \\
`[The word] ɲɯ-ɣɤ-mdzu means `it has thorns', it does not [specify whether] there are many or not.' (elicited)
exe

Another meaning of the ɣɤ- prefix is `from which $X$ comes out, emitting $X$'. For instance ɣɤrdɯlbe dusty has the specific meaning `emitting dust' (of a dusty road) rather than `be covered in dust' (see § sec:denom.GA.pairing ). The verb ɣɤkʰɯ (from tɤ-kʰɯsmoke) has two different meanings: `be smoky' (of a place) or `have smoke coming out' ( ex:kha.YWGAkhWnW ).

exe

kʰa ɲɯ-ɣɤ-kʰɯ-nɯ \\
house sens - denom -smoke- pl \\
`There is smoke coming out from their house.' (2012 Norbzang) 0003768#S194
exe

Among these verbs, ɣɤtɕabe wrong is one of the few intransitive verbs that can be reflexivized with the ʑɣɤ- prefix (§ sec:refl.intr ), with a reflexive tropative meaning ʑɣɤɣɤtɕarecognize one's mistake.

Some ɣɤ- denominal verbs are clearly dynamic verbs. For instance, the denominal ɣɤtsɯrhave cracks ( ex:loGAtsWr ) has the same meaning as the collocation combining the base noun tɤ-tsɯrcrack with the verb ɕego ( ex:WtsWr.loCe ).

exe

xlist

ɯ-rnom-ɕɤrɯ lo-ɣɤ-tsɯr \\
3sg. poss -rib-bone ifr: upstream - denom -crack \\

ɯ-rnom-ɕɤrɯ ɣɯ ɯ-tsɯr lo-ɕe \\
3sg. poss -rib-bone gen 3sg. poss -crack ifr: upstream -go \\
`His ribs got fractured.' (elicited)
xlist
exe

Some of the dynamic intransitive denominal verbs in ɣɤ- such as ɣɤtsɯrhave cracks and ɣɤwucry have patientive intransitive subjects, but a few other verbs such as ɣɤrʁaʁhunt and ɣɯɕoŋtɕachop timber have agentive subjects like the transitive denominal ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- verbs treated in the following section.

The intransitive deideophonic ɣɤ- prefix (§ sec:GA.sA.deidph ) is probably historically related to the ɣɤ- intransitive denominal prefix.
summary:
The ɣɤ- prefix derives several kinds of intransitive verbs, including stative proprietive verbs like “be muddy,” with bases that may be possessed nouns, nouns with frozen prefixes, property nouns, or even abstract nouns. Its meaning differs slightly from aɣɯ-, which typically means ‘have a lot of X’ or ‘produce a lot of X,’ whereas ɣɤ- usually means simply ‘have X,’ and it can also express meanings such as ‘emit X’ or, in some cases, dynamic actions.

The passage also shows that nouns in the same semantic class may take different denominal prefixes, and some bases can form verbs with both ɣɤ- and aɣɯ- but with different meanings. A few ɣɤ- verbs are reflexivized, some are patientive or agentive intransitives, and the intransitive deideophonic

text:
The ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- prefix can also derive transitive verbs, either from inalienably possessed nouns or counted nouns (see tab:denom.GA.intr ). The correlation between the vocalism of the indefinite possessor prefix tɯ-/tɤ- and that of the denominal prefix ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- is less consistent than for other derivations.

The verb ɣɤxpradispatch has the unique allomorph ɣɤx- with an intrusive velar fricative -x- like some voice derivations (§ sec:caus.sWG ), even though this is not found in the base noun tɤpramessenger and the other denominal verb nɤprabe dispatched (§ sec:denom.GA.pairing ).

When the base noun refers to a concrete object, the corresponding ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- denominal verb expresses the action prototypically associated with the use of that object, for instance ɣɯrithread (pass a thread through beads/a needle's eye) from tɤ-rithread.

Denominal verbs in ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- have meanings that are close to those of highly lexically-specific noun-verb collocations, and the correspondences between the argument structures of the denominal verbs and those of the corresponding collocations are not uniform.

For instance, the verb ɣɯtɕʰaanswer is semantically close to the complex predicate involving the base noun tɯ-tɕʰainformation, news and the ditransitive verb kʰogive, and the recipient (person who receives an answer to his message) is encoded as the possessor of the inalienably possessed noun tɯ-tɕʰa in the collocation ( ex:atCha.mWnakho, § sec:biactantial.ipn ), and as direct object of the denominal ɣɯtɕʰa. However, the possessor of the base noun does not necessarily always correspond to the object of the ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- denominal verb. For example, in the case of the transitive verb ɣɤjmŋodream of and its near-synonymous collocation tɯ-jmŋo+ntɕʰɤr `appear in $X$'s dream' (from tɯ-jmŋodream with the intransitive verb ntɕʰɤrappear), the possessor of the base noun tɯ-jmŋo encodes the experiencer (the person dreaming), corresponding to the transitive subject of ɣɤjmŋo as in ( ex:pWGAjmNota ).

exe

[aʑo [...] qartsʰi ɲɤ-k-ɤpa-a-ci] pɯ-ɣɤ-jmŋo-t-a \\
1sg cricket ifr - peg -become- 1sg - peg aor - denom -dream- pst: tr - 1sg \\
`I dreamed that I had become a cricket.' (150904 cuzhi-zh)
0006322#S178
exe

Some transitive ɣɯ- denominal verbs can be subjected to the a- passive derivation (§ sec:passive ). The resulting verbs, for instance aɣɯɕkatbe loaded with ( ex:aGWCkat ), superficially resemble aɣɯ- proprietive denominal verbs (§ sec:denom.aGW ), and it is possible that the aɣɯ- derivation originates from a combination of the passive with the transitive denominal ɣɯ-.

exe

ki tɤrka ki tɤ-rɤku a-ɣɯ-ɕkat \\
dem. prox mule dem. prox indef. poss -crop pass - denom - load: fact \\
`This mule has been loaded with (burdens containing) crops.' (elicited)
exe

The ɣɤ-/ɣɯ- denominal prefix is cognate with Tshobdun wɐ, for instance wɐ-riʔ `thread a needle' from riʔ `thread',, which exactly corresponds to Japhug ɣɯrithread.
summary: The ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- prefix can form transitive verbs from inalienably possessed nouns or counted nouns, but the relation between the vowel of the base noun’s possessor prefix and the denominal prefix is less regular than in other derivations. These verbs often denote the action typically associated with a concrete object, and their argument structure may resemble that of closely related noun-verb collocations, though the correspondence is not consistent; in some cases the possessor of the base noun becomes the object of the derived verb, while in others it corresponds to the subject. The passage also notes that some transitive ɣɯ- denominal verbs can take an a- passive and that the prefix is cognate with Tshobdun wɐ.

text:
denominal derivation!pairing
A considerable number of nouns can take both ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- and nɯ-/nɤ- denominal prefixes. tab:denom.GA.nA presents a list of pairs of denominal verbs derived with these prefixes; the base nouns are not included in this table for lack of space, but are indicated in Tables tab:denom.GA.intr and tab:denom.GA.tr above.

These pairs can be classified into three groups, depending on the transitivity of the verbs and the semantic correspondences between them.

First, we find pairs of intransitive verbs, where the ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- verb expresses either a property associated with a place (`have $X$', `emitting $X$'), or with a dummy intransitive subject ( ɣɤndʐobe cold), while the nɯ-/nɤ- denominal verbs takes as subject an experiencer ( nɤndʐofeel cold).

In the case of the pair of intransitive verbs ɣɤrdɯl and nɯrdɯl (from rdɯldust) however, the subject of nɯrdɯl is not an experiencer, the semantic difference between the two verbs being explained in ( ex:GArdWl.def ).

exe

kɯ-ɣɤ-rdɯl nɯ, ɯʑo ɯ-taʁ rdɯl tu-kɯ-ɬoʁ nɯ ŋu, kɯ-nɯ-rdɯl nɯ, ɯʑo ɯ-taʁ rdɯl kɤ-kɯ-ndzoʁ nɯ ŋu \\
inf: stat - denom -dust dem 3sg 3sg. poss -on dust ipfv: up - sbj: pcp -come.out dem be: fact inf: stat - denom -dust dem 3sg 3sg. poss -on dust aor - sbj: pcp - acaus:attach dem be: fact \\
` kɯ-ɣɤ-rdɯl means that dust is coming up from it, and kɯ-nɯ-rdɯl means that dust is attached on it.' (elicited definition)
exe

Second, there are cases in which the ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- denominal verb is intransitive, and the corresponding nɯ-/nɤ- verb is transitive, such as ɣɤwucry and nɤwucry for. The transitive subject of the nɯ-/nɤ- verb corresponds to the same entity as the intransitive subject of its counterpart in ɣɯ-/ɣɤ, and has the same functional relationship to it as an applicative derivation (§ sec:applicative ) to its base verb, as the object of the transitive verb in nɯ-/nɤ- expresses a patientive argument.

Third, the opposite situation, with transitive denominal verbs in ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- and intransitive verbs in nɯ-/nɤ, is also attested. These are passive-like configurations, where the subject of the intransitive verb corresponds to the object of its transitive counterpart (as in ɣɤxpradispatch / nɤprabe dispatched), and antipassive-like configurations, where the subjects of both verbs are the same ( ɣɯɕkatload / nɯɕkatcarry loads).
summary: The passage notes that many nouns can form denominal verbs with either ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- or nɯ-/nɤ- prefixes, and these paired verbs fall into three groups based on transitivity and meaning. In some pairs, both verbs are intransitive but differ in whether the subject is a dummy, a property-holder, or an experiencer; in others, the ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- verb is intransitive while the nɯ-/nɤ- verb is transitive; and in the third type, the pattern is reversed, yielding either passive-like or antipassive-like semantic relations.

text:
The most common function of the mɤ- denominal prefix to derive intransitive verbs of relative location from locative relator nouns (§ sec:other.locative.relator ), as illustrated in tab:mA.denom.location. Note the presence of Tibetan loanwords in this list, including ɯ-pɕioutside and ɯ-χcɤlcenter from ཕྱི་pʰʲioutside and
དཀྱིལ་dkʲilcenter, a fact that demonstrates the productivity of this derivation. The first syllable of ɯ-pɤrtʰɤβbetween is also borrowed from བར་barspace between.

The mɤ- denominal prefix is possibly related to the maŋ- prefix which derives verbs of relative locations from locational adverbs, for instance maŋlobe upstream from loupstream (§ sec:verbs.relative.location ).

In addition to their semantic similarity, verbs of location in mɤ- and maŋ- have in common the fact that they are among the very few intransitive verbs that can be reflexivized (§ sec:refl.intr ): ʑɣɤ- prefixation yields volitional motion verbs such as ʑɣɤmɤpɤrtʰɤβput oneself in between or ʑɣɤmaŋloput oneself upstream, from mɤpɤrtʰɤβbe in the middle and maŋlobe upstream.

The causativization of mɤ- denominal verbs has several outcomes. With mɤkube first and maqʰube after, which can have temporal meanings (§ sec:ordinals ), the sigmatic causative forms z-mɤku and z-maqʰu generally mean `do first' or `do after/later' with complement clauses as in ( ex:Wthu.tAtWzmAkut ) (see also examples ex:pWzmAke, § sec:sig.caus.serial and ex:YWGAmda § sec:facilitative.GA ).

exe

sɯlɤmgrɯβdɤn kɯ [ɯ-tʰu] tɤ-tɯ-z-mɤku-t ŋu tɕe \\
anthr erg 3sg. poss - bare. inf:ask aor -2- caus -be.first- pst: tr be: fact lnk \\
`Bsod.nam sgrub.ldan, you were the first to ask [her hand in marriage].' (sras 2003)
exe

The causative z-maqʰu also has the straightforward causative meaning `cause to be late, delay' (examples ex:tha.kWzmaqhutCi, § sec:incl.semi.reflexive and ex:YWwGzmaqhu, § sec:obviation.animacy ).

With other verbs, for which a temporal interpretation is not possible, the causative derivation means `put in $X$', where $X$ corresponds to the relator noun. For instance, z-mɤŋgɯ and z-mɤpɕi occur in the sense of `wear (some clothes) inside' and `wear outside'. In addition, z-mɤpɕi can be used in the metaphorical sense of `treat as a stranger'.

In addition to generating verbs of relative location, the denominal mɯ- and mɤ- prefixes are also attested with other functions, illustrated by the examples in tab:mA.denom2.

First, they derive stative intransitive verbs of quantity or size such a mɤlɯmbe big in size from tɯ-lɯmsize. Most of the examples in this category are highly lexicalized: mɯstibe alone derives from the stem --sti `alone' which is only used in the Kamnyu dialect in compounds with pronouns as first element (§ sec:stWsti ) or as the reduplicated adverb stɯstialone, and mɤmube the most important, is presumably derived from tɤ-mumother, though not by a direct semantic change.

To these examples, it is possible to add mɤmbɯrprotruding, which probably comes from a lost noun *mbɯr borrowed from Tibetan འབུར་ⁿburbulge, protuberance, and mɯxtebe the majority, which may originate from the obsolete property noun *ɯ-te `big' (§ sec:augmentative ), though there is also the possibility of an isolated derivation from wxtibe big with ablaut (see for instance the form -xte in the compound noun xtɕɯxtesize, § sec.v.v.compounds.degree and § sec:denom.a above).

Second, the mɤ- prefix is used to build intransitive verbs meaning `become someone's $X$' from kinship terms, as in mɤrʑaβmarry (of a girl) and mɤtɕɯbe adopted as a son This verb has the additional meaning of Chinese 入赘 rùzhuìmarry into one's wife's household. from tɤ-rʑaβwife and tɤ-tɕɯson, respectively.

Third, there is one transitive verb derived with the mɤ- prefix: mɤrpaʁcarry on the shoulder from the inalienably possessed body part tɯ-rpaʁshoulder, anomalous both because of the vocalism of the denominal prefix ( mɯ- is expected) and because of its isolated meaning, similar to the nɤ- denominal verb nɤrpaʁcarry on the shoulder (§ sec:denom.tr.nW ).
summary:
The passage describes the productive mɤ- denominal prefix, which most commonly derives intransitive verbs of relative location from locative relator nouns, and notes that some of these forms include Tibetan loanwords. It also says mɤ- may be related to the maŋ- prefix, since both form location verbs that can be reflexivized with ʑɣɤ- to express volitional motion.

It then explains that causativized mɤ- verbs can mean either ‘do first/after’ with temporal expressions, ‘cause to be late,’ or, with other verbs, ‘put in X’ where X is the relator noun. Finally, the passage lists additional less common uses of mɤ-/mɯ-, including deriving stative verbs of size or quantity, verbs meaning ‘become someone’s X’ from kinship terms, and one isolated transitive verb meaning ‘carry on the shoulder.’

text: The denominal prefixes nɯ-/nɤ- have a high degree of productivity, and present a wide range of functions. They can derive both intransitive and transitive verbs from nouns.
summary: The denominal prefixes nɯ-/nɤ- are highly productive and serve a wide range of functions. In particular, they can derive both intransitive and transitive verbs from nouns.

text:
Intransitive denominal derivations in nɯ-/nɤ- have at least six different meanings, illustrated in tab:denom.nA.intr. All six categories contain examples of borrowings from Tibetan and even Chinese in some cases, such as ɯ-mdoʁcolour, rdɯldust and χpɯnbumaster from མདོག་mdogcolour, རྡུལ་rduldust and དཔོན་པོ་dpon.polord, respectively.

First, some denominal verbs in nV- are stative, including proprietive verbs like nɤmarbe oily from ta-marbutter, with a meaning quite different from aɣɯmarproduce a lot of butter with the aɣɯ- prefix (§ sec:denom.aGW ). Borrowed Chinese adjectives taking the nɯ- prefix (§ sec:zh.loanverbs ) also belong to this category.

Among these stative verbs, nɯmdoʁlook like from ɯ-mdoʁcolour is semi-transitive, as shown by ( ex:pjAnWmdoR ), where its semi-object is the headless relative ɯ-sni mɤ-kɯ-ɲaʁ `who is not evil (whose heart is not black)'.

exe

<maji> nɯnɯ [ɯ-sni mɤ-kɯ-ɲaʁ] pjɤ-nɯ-mdoʁ \\
anthr dem 3sg. poss -heart neg - sbj: pcp -be.black pst. ifr - denom -colour \\
`Ma Ji looked like someone who was not evil.' (160702 luocha) 0006135#S45
exe

The ability of this verb to take a semi-object derives from the grammaticalized use of ɯ-mdoʁcolour as a complement-taking nominal predicate meaning `it looks like...' (§ sec:WmdoR.TAME ). This is one of the few cases where the synthetic construction corresponding to a denominal derivation is not a noun+verb complex predicate (§ sec:denominal.vs.light.verb ).

Second, the nɯ-/nɤ- denominal derivation can mean `get (covered by) $X$, suffer from $X$', as in nɯɣursuffer from frost (from tɯɣurfrost). This verb selects as subject plants ( ex:pWnWGur ), and differs from the corresponding light verb construction tɯɣur+ta ( ex:tWGur.pata ) (§ sec:ta.lv ) whose transitive subject is dummy (§ sec:transitive.dummy ).

exe

stonka tɕe li, nɤki, pɯ-nɯ-ɣur qʰe, li pjɯ-tsɣi qʰe mɯ-ɲɯ-sna ɕti. \\
autumn lnk again filler aor - denom -frost lnk again ipfv -rot lnk neg - ipfv -be.good be. aff: fact \\
`In autumn, when [the Arisaema consanguineum ] get frosted, it rots and dies.' (14-sWNgWJu)
0003506#S166
exe

exe

tɯɣur pa-ta, kɯ-dɤn ʑo mɯ-pa-ta. \\
frost aor:3 3-put sbj: pcp -be.many emph neg - aor:3 3-put \\
`There was a bit of frost, but not much.' (conversation, 15-12-17)
exe

Third, the nɯ-/nɤ- denominal prefixes can also derive verbs of motion towards a location, such as nɤχcɤlgo to the center (from ɯ-χcɤlcenter). These verbs differ from the verbs of location derived with the mɤ- prefix such as mɤχcɤlbe in the center, which express a static position without motion ( tab:mA.denom.location, § sec:denom.mA ).

Fourth, these prefixes can be used to build verbs describing an activity related to the base noun. The denominal verbs can have the same meaning as a light verb construction in βzumake, as in the case of nɯrɤɣosing (§ sec:preverb.speech ) and rɤɣo+βzu `sing'. Alternatively, the corresponding complex predicate can be an existential construction (§ sec:existential.light.verbs ): compare the use of the denominal verb nɯsaχsɯhave lunch in ( ex:tAtWnWsaXsW ) with that of the base noun saχsɯlunch combined with the existential verb tuexist in ( ex:saXsW.WpWtu ).

exe

xlist

ɯ-tɤ́-tɯ-nɯ-saχsɯ? \\
qu - aor -2- denom -lunch \\

nɤ-saχsɯ ɯ-pɯ́-tu? \\
3sg. poss -lunch qu - pst. ipfv -exist \\
`Did you have lunch?' (both heard in context several times)
xlist
exe

The rɯ-/rɤ- denominal prefix is more commonly used for these meanings (in examples such as rɯndzɤtsʰihave a meal from ndzɤtsʰimeal, § sec:denom.intr.rA ), and the choice between the nasal and the rhotic denominal prefixes is lexically determined.

Fifth, when the base noun expresses a profession or social status, the denominal verb in nɯ- means `become $X$' ( ex:lAnWXpWnbu ), synonymous with the light verb construction with ndotake (§ sec:ndo.lv ) as in ( ex:XpWnbu.lando ).

exe

xlist

jaʁmɤcʰɯqa lɤ-nɯ-χpɯnbu \\
anthr aor: upstream - denom -master \\
`Yagmakhyiqa became the master.' (2003-kWBRa)

χpɯnbu la-ndo \\
master aor:3 3: upstream -take \\
`He became the master.' (elicited)
xlist
exe

The rhotic prefixes also appear in this function, though only on two nouns: χpɯnmonk and tɕɤmɯnun ( rɤχpɯnbecome a monk and rɯtɕɤmɯbecome a nun, § sec:denom.intr.rA ). Using the nɯ- denominal prefix instead of the rhotic prefixes with these two nouns is not ungrammatical, but less unfelicitous.

The verb nɯʁjoʁ from ʁjoʁservant is labile, and means `work as a servant' in intransitive use (see § sec:lability.pass and § sec:denom.tr.nW for further discussion).

Sixth, when the base noun designates an animal or a plant, the nɯ-/nɤ- prefix most often means `search/look for/collect $X$-. This highly productive function corresponds semantically to the combination with the verb pʰɯttake out, cut in the case of plants: in ( ex:kWnWmtshalu ) for instance, the same action is redundantly referred to by the verb nɯmtsʰalusearch for nettle and by mtsʰalunettle followed by pʰɯt.

exe

kɯ-nɯ-mtsʰalu, mtsʰalu ɯ-kɯ-pʰɯt jo-ɣi \\
sbj: pcp - denom -nettle nettle 3sg. poss - sbj: pcp -take.out ifr -come \\
`She came to collect nettle.' (140520 ye tiane-zh)
0004044#S345
exe

When the base noun refers to animal, this denominal derivation has the same meaning as the verb tɕɤttake out, `extract' as shown by ( ex:kWnWqaJy ) where both constructions redundantly occur.

exe

lu-fsoʁ ɕɯŋgɯ tɕe tɕendɤre kɯ-nɯ-qaɟy ntsɯ ju-ɕe pjɤ-ŋu. tɕendɤre qaɟy ntsɯ ʑ-lu-tɕɤt pjɤ-ŋu tɕe, \\
ipfv -be.day before lnk lnk sbj: pcp - denom -fish always ipfv -go ifr. ipfv -be lnk fish always tral - ipfv: upstream -take.out ifr. ipfv -be lnk \\
`[The fisherman] always went fishing before daybreak.' (140512 yufu yu mogui)
0003973#S8
exe

Like the rhotic prefix, the nɯ- denominal prefix also has a deadverbial function, and occurs in nɯʁlɤwɯrdo suddenly from ʁlɤwɯrsuddenly (compare with rɯʁlɤwɯrhappen suddenly, § sec:denom.intr.rA ).

A possible irregular reduced allomorph n- of the intransitive denominal nɯ- prefix is possibly found in the verb ngobe ill, which is derived from the inalienably possessed noun tɯ-ŋgodisease: the group ng- represents nŋg- phonologically (§ sec:NC.clusters ). This irregular allomorph appears to also be attested with some transitive verbs (§ sec:denom.tr.nW ).
summary: The intransitive denominal prefixes nɯ-/nɤ- have at least six meanings: they can form stative verbs, verbs meaning ‘get covered by / suffer from X,’ motion-toward verbs, activity verbs related to the noun, ‘become X’ verbs from profession or status nouns, and productive verbs meaning ‘search/look for/collect X’ from animal or plant nouns. The passage also notes special cases such as semi-transitive stative uses, labile verbs, deadverbial uses, and a possible irregular reduced allomorph n-, while showing that some meanings overlap with light-verb constructions and may be lexically determined.

text:
The nɯ-/nɤ- denominal prefix is also used to derive transitive verbs, with a considerable variety of meanings, all with high productivity. In the following, in order to clarify the glosses, $X$ represents the base noun, and $Y$ the object of the corresponding transitive nɯ-/nɤ- denominal verb.

First, transitive denominal verbs in nɯ-/nɤ- can have a tropative function `treat/consider $Y$ as $X$', as in the case of nɯʁgratreat as an enemy from ʁgraenemy. The verb nɯʁjoʁ `give orders to' (from `treat as a servant') from ʁjoʁservant is labile, and means `work as a servant' when conjugated intransitively. It is one of the very few verbs with ergative lability in Japhug (see § sec:lability.pass ).

The opposite (anti-tropative) meaning `be treated as $X$ by $Y$' is found in nɤmebe adopted as a daughter (from tɯ-medaughter: `become $Y$'s daughter'), the transitive equivalent of the mɤ- derivation found in the intransitive verb mɤtɕɯbe adopted as a son (from tɤ-tɕɯson, § sec:denom.mA ).

Second, the transitive nɯ-/nɤ- denominal has an instrumental function like the sigmatic denominal (§ sec:denom.sW.caus.instr ). This function can be subdivided into two cases: `use $X$ to do to $Y$' as in nɤtarhit with a stick (selecting the entity being hit as object) from tɤtarstick and `use $Y$ as an $X$' as in nɤɲiuse as a walking stick from tɤɲiwalking stick (selecting as object the implement used to replace a walking stick, as shown by ex:tonAYi ).

exe

ɯ-rkoŋtoŋ nɯnɯ ci to-ndo tɕe to-nɤ-ɲi tɕe \\
3sg. poss -femur dem indef ifr -take lnk ifr - denom -walking.stick lnk \\
`He picked one of its femurs up and used it as a walking stick.' (140511 xinbada-zh)
0003961#S70
exe

Third, when the base noun refers to the body part (or a substance coming from) of a plant or an animal, the denominal verb can mean `take the $Y$ from the $X$', the object $X$ being the possessor of that body part. The meaning of this derivation is similar to that of the verbs pʰɯttake out, cut and tɕɤttake out with the corresponding base nouns: The same is true of the intransitive denominal verbs in nɯ-/nɤ- meaning `search/look for/collect $X$' discussed above. for instance, nɤrmeremove the hair (shear) expresses the same meaning as tɤ-rmehair with pʰɯt in example ( ex:chWnArme ).

exe

nɯŋa kɯ-fse, qaʑo kɯ-fse nɯra cʰɯ-nɤ-rme ŋgrɤl. nɯnɯ ɯ-rme cʰɯ-pʰɯt ŋgrɤl ma, \\
cow sbj: pcp -be.like sheep sbj: pcp -be.like dem: pl ipfv: downstream - denom: tr -hair be.usually.the.case: fact dem 3sg. poss -hair ipfv: downstream -take.off be.usually.the.case: fact lnk \\
`[Bats] remove the hair of cows and sheep, they remove their hair.' (25-qarmWrwa)
0003648#S16
exe

With the counted noun tɯ-rdoʁone piece (§ sec:CN.distributive ) the transitive denominal derivation yields the distributed action meaning nɯrdoʁ `pick up one by one'.

Fourth, when the base noun is an abstract noun, the transitive denominal in nɯ-/nɤ- expresses an action directed toward a patient or stimulus, as in nɤmbrɯget angry with (from
tɤ-mbrɯanger, see also § sec:denom.sA.proprietive ). Among these verbs, nɤre `laugh, laugh at, mock' from the inalienably possessed noun tɤ-relaugh (n) is labile (§ sec:lability.apass ).

Fifth, denominal verbs in nɯ- can have idiosyncratic meanings associated with a noun+verb collocation. For instance nɯskʰrɯbe pregnant with ( ex:tonWkrAzndZi, § sec:denom.rA.pairing ) from tɯ-skʰrɯbody derives from the collocation tɯ-skʰrɯ+NEG+βdi `be pregnant' (§ sec:other.collocation.intr ), but it did not integrate the verbal root βdibe well and the negative prefix.

Irregular allomorphs of the transitive denominal nɯ- prefix include the reduced form n- in ntsɣesell from tɯtsɣecommerce (§ sec:antipassive.irr.form, and nɯN- with an intrusive homorganic nasal in the transitive motion verb nɯɴqʰugo along, follow (§ sec:motion.verbs ) which derives from ɯ-qʰuafter, behind.
summary: The nɯ-/nɤ- denominal prefix productively derives transitive verbs from nouns with several distinct meanings. These include tropative and anti-tropative uses (‘treat/consider as X’ and ‘be treated as X by Y’), instrumental uses (‘use X to do to Y’ or ‘use Y as an X’), part-removal meanings from body-part nouns, distributed-action meanings, and verbs directed toward an abstract patient or stimulus; some forms are also labile. The passage also notes a few idiosyncratic meanings tied to noun-verb collocations and mentions irregular allomorphs of the prefix.

text:
denominal derivation!pairing
The nV- denominal prefixes are most commonly paired with rV- prefixes (§ sec:denom.rA.pairing ). When a transitive nV- denominal verb (§ sec:denom.tr.nW ) occurs in pair with an intransitive rV- verb (§ sec:denom.intr.rA ), for instance nɯkrɤzdiscuss vs. rɤkrɤzhave a discussion, the intransitive verb serves as the functional antipassive of the transitive one, and the nV- verb cannot take the antipassive rɤ- prefix (§ sec:antipassive.vs.denominal.pairs ).

The nɤ- denominal prefix also derives dynamic verbs (both transitive and intransitive) paired with proprietive denominal verbs in sɤ- (§ sec:denom.sA.proprietive ).

These verbs are not compatible with the proprietive sɤ- derivation (§ sec:proprietive ): the corresponding stative sɤ- denominal is used instead. For instance, the transitive denominal verb nɤŋaβconsider to be unpleasant, `be embarrassed by' (from tɤŋaβunpleasant thing, wrong) lacks a proprietive form such as $ $ sɤ-nɤŋaβ, and the denominal sɤŋaβbe unpleasant, `be embarrassing' ( ex:sANAB in § sec:denom.sA.proprietive ) is used instead.

Denominal verbs in nɤ- can however take the sɤ- antipassive prefix (§ sec:antipassive.sA ), for example sɤnɤrelaugh at people from nɤrelaugh (§ sec:lability.apass ).

Some sɤ-/nɤ- denominal pairs have lost their base noun. For instance, there is no abstract noun $ $ tɤɕqa in Kamnyu Japhug corresponding to the pair sɤɕqabe bearable/ nɤɕqaendure. Nevertheless, like synchronic denominal verbs such as nɤŋaβconsider to be unpleasant, the transitive form in these pairs cannot undergo the proprietive derivation: the denominal sɤɕqa ( ex:mAkWsACqa ) is used instead of a putative form such as $ $ sɤ-nɤɕqa.

exe

a-χpɯm ɲɯ-mŋɤm ri, mɤ-kɯ-sɤɕqa maŋe \\
1sg. poss -knee sens -hurt lnk neg - sbj: pcp -be.bearable not.exist: sens \\
`My knee hurts, but nothing unbearable.' (elicited)
exe

Pairing with other denominal prefixes such as ɣɯ-/ɣɤ- (§ sec:denom.tr.GA ) is also attested, but with less straightforward semantic correspondences between the two verbs.
summary:
The nV- denominal prefixes are most often paired with rV- prefixes, where the rV- verb functions as the antipassive of the transitive nV- verb and blocks the nV- form from taking the rɤ- antipassive prefix. The nɤ- prefix also forms dynamic transitive and intransitive verbs that pair with proprietive sɤ- verbs, but these verbs do not themselves take proprietive sɤ- derivation; instead, a separate stative sɤ- denominal form is used.

Some sɤ-/nɤ- pairs have lost their original noun base, yet the same restriction against proprietive derivation still applies. Pairings with other denominal prefixes, such as ɣɯ-/ɣɤ-, are also found, though their semantic relations are less regular.

text:
denominal derivation!zero-derivation zero-derivation!denominal backformation
While there are non-finite verbs and deverbal nouns lacking any specific nominalization affix (bare infinitives § sec:bare.inf and bare action nominals § sec:bare.action.nominals ), there is little evidence in Japhug for denominal zero-derivation.

tab:verb.backformation includes cases of noun-verb pairs in which the semantics of the verb is innovative: the nouns have the same meanings as those of their cognates in other Trans-Himalayan languages such as Chinese and Tibetan (for evidence that these nouns are not borrowed from Tibetan, see and ), but there is no trace of the corresponding verbs outside of core Gyalrong languages.

The inalienably possessed nouns ta-marbutter, tɤ-mkɯmpillow and tɤjpɣomice formally look like bare nominalizations (§ sec:tA.abstract.nouns, § sec:bare.action.nominals ) from the corresponding verbs. The etymological relationship between ta-marbutter and marsmear, while not completely obvious, is supported by the existence of the figura etymologica in ( ex:kumarnW ) and the typological parallel provided by the French denominal verb beurrer `smear' (not necessarily butter) from beurre `butter'.

exe

ta-mar ʁɟa ʑo ku-mar-nɯ \\
indef. poss -butter completely emph ipfv -smear- pl \\
`They smeared it completely with butter.' (30-komar)
0003738#S11
exe

The inalienably possessed noun tɤ-mkɯmpillow is related to the rare orienting verb (§ sec:orienting.verbs ) mkɯm `have one's head turned towards $X$ while lying in bed', as in ( ex:chWmkWm ).

exe

tɤ-tɕɯ nɯ, soz tɕe, rɤru tɤkʰa tɕe, tɕʰeme nɯ ɣɯ [...] ɯ-jme pɕoʁ nɯtɕu ntsɯ cʰɯ-mkɯm pjɤ-ŋu \\
indef. poss -son dem morning loc get.up: fact moment loc girl dem gen 3sg. poss -tail side dem: loc always ipfv: downstream -head.towards ifr. ipfv -be \\
`The man, in the morning, when he was about to get up, had his head towards the tail of the woman.' (rkoNrJAl2002)
exe

In both cases, the cognates in Chinese and Tibetan suggest that the verbs in Japhug are secondary. I propose that rather than being cases of denominal zero-derivation, these verbs were back-formed from the nouns on the model of bare nominalizations.

The case of the verb ndzom `form a bridge of ice (over a body of water)' ( ex:kondzom ) is more puzzling, since the noun ndzombridge from which this verb originates is alienably possessed and does not have a frozen tɤ- prefix. There is no model from which this verb could have been backformed.

exe

tɯ-ci ko-ndzom \\
indef. poss -water ifr -form.a.bridge.of.ice \\
`A bridge of ice formed over the river.' (elicited)
exe

A possible scenario for the backformation hypothesis is that a nɯ- denominal verb (§ sec:denom.nW ) was first derived from the base noun, and its nɯ- prefix was then reinterpreted as an autive prefix (§ sec:autobenefactive ). Both the spontaneous (§ sec:autoben.spontaneous ) and the permansive (§ sec:autoben.permansive ) functions of the autive would be compatible with the meaning of the verb ndzom `form a bridge of ice'. As a consequence of this backformation, a prefixless verb, whose stem is identical to that of the base noun, was created, following the pathway in ( ex:nW.backformation ).

exe

ndzom $ $ *nɯ-ndzom $ $ *nɯ-ndzom $ $ ndzom \\
bridge $ $ * denom -bridge $ $ * auto -form.a.bridge $ $ form.a.bridge \\
exe

A synchronic example of ongoing reanalysis of the nɯ- denominal prefix as an autive prefix is provided by the transitive verb nɯmɢlastep over, `cross', which derives from the counted noun tɯ-mɢlaone step. An anomalous form ja-mɢla ( ex:jamGla ) without the nɯ- prefix is found in the corpus, and can be explained as having been backformed from ja-nɯ-mɢla (see ex:jannWpGaRndZi.jannWmGlandZi, § sec:motion.verbs, with a similar context) by this mechanism.

exe

rirɤβ tʰɤstɯɣ ja-pɣaʁ, tɯ-ci tʰɤstɯɣ ja-mɢla mɤ-xsi ma, \\
mountain how.many aor:3 -cross indef. poss -water how.many aor:3 -step.over neg - genr:know lnk \\
`It is not now how many mountains and rivers he crossed.' (160706 poucet6)
0006109#S44
exe
summary: The passage argues that Japhug shows little evidence for denominal zero-derivation, and instead many apparent noun–verb pairs are better analyzed as backformations from nouns, especially where the verb meanings are innovative and lack cognates outside core Gyalrong. Examples such as *ta-mar* ‘butter’ and *tɤ-mkɯm* ‘pillow’ suggest verbs were created from bare nominal-like forms, while the case of *ndzom* ‘form a bridge of ice’ is explained as a possible reanalysis of an earlier denominal form with an *nɯ-* prefix.

text:
denominal derivation!vowel alternation vowel!alternation alternation!vowel
The inalienably possessed noun ɯ-fsuof the same size, used in one of the equative constructions (§ sec:Wfsu.equative, § sec:3sg.possessive.form, ), is etymologically related to the stative verb fsebe like. This u / e alternation, which is similar to that of Stem III (§ sec:stem3.form ) and a few other isolated examples (§ sec:pWrndeta ), is possibly due to a *-j suffix.
summary: The inalienably possessed noun **ɯ-fsuo** ‘the same size,’ used in an equative construction, is etymologically related to the stative verb **fsebe** ‘like.’ Its **u/e alternation** resembles that found in Stem III and a few other isolated cases, and it may be explained by a historical **\*-j suffix**.

text:
derivation!ideophone to verb deideophonic derivation ideophone!verb
In addition to nouns (and some adverbs such as ʁlɤwɯrsuddenly, § sec:denom.intr.rA ), some verbalizing prefixes can take ideophones as input.

ɣɤ- and sɤ- deideophonic verbs
The most productive deideophonic prefixes are ɣɤ- and sɤ-. Verbs derived with these prefixes can be built from most (though not all) ideophonic roots, either from the reduplicated root (type I) or from a root with partial reduplication in l- (type II).

Type I deideophonic verbs can be illustrated by the intransitive verb ɣɤplaʁplaʁ `flick, extend and retract' (of a snake's tongue) ( ex:YWGAplaRplaR ) and its transitive counterpart sɤplaʁplaʁ ( ex:YWsAplaRplaR ).

exe

xlist

qapri ɣɯ ɯ-mdʑu ɲɯ-ɣɤ-plaʁplaʁ ʑo \\
snake gen 3sg. poss -tongue sens - deiph: intr -flicking emph \\
`The snake's tongue is flicking.' (elicited)

qapri kɯ ɯ-mdʑu ɲɯ-sɤ-plaʁplaʁ ʑo \\
snake erg 3sg. poss -tongue sens - deiph: tr -flicking emph \\
`The snake is flicking its tongue.' (elicited)
xlist
exe

Despite the fact that the reduplicated root -plaʁplaʁ in these verbs resembles the type II ideophonic pattern (which has a stative meaning, § sec:ideo.II ), its meaning corresponds to that of the type III pattern `dynamic action' ideophone, namely plaʁnɤplaʁflickering (§ sec:ideo.III ). The type II pattern plaʁplaʁ of the ideophonic root -plaʁ has a entirely unrelated meaning: `completely white'. Compare ( ex:YWsAplaRplaR ) with the corresponding light verb construction ( ex:plaRnAplaR.YAsWstu ), which uses the similative verb studo like (§ sec:stu.idph ). In this particular case, the deideophonic verb in ( ex:YWsAplaRplaR ) expresses a faster motion than the construction in ( ex:plaRnAplaR.YAsWstu ), but this semantic difference is not generalizable to all deideophonic verbs.

exe

qapri kɯ ɯ-mdʑu plaʁnɤplaʁ ʑo ɲɯ-ɤsɯ-stu \\
snake erg 3sg. poss -tongue idph (III):flickering emph sens - prog -do.like \\
`The snake is flicking its tongue.' (elicited)
exe

As a general rule, type I verbs in ɣɤ- and sɤ- have a meaning that corresponds to that of the type III ideophone based on the same root. They differ from each other in that the prefix ɣɤ- builds intransitive verbs, whose synthetic counterpart is a light verb construction with an intransitive verb such as ʑɣɤstu `act like' (§ sec:stu.idph ), whereas sɤ- derives transitive verbs with a causative meaning `make $X$ do/be' like the construction with studo like ( ex:plaRnAplaR.YAsWstu ).

Type II deideophonic verbs have partial reduplication of the ideophonic root in l, and semantically correspond to pattern IV (§ sec:ideo.IV ), expressing spatially distributed action (note that the distributed action derivation also presents the l- reduplication, § sec:distributed.action ). Most ideophonic roots either derive type I or type II deideophonic verbs. For instance, there is no verb $ $ ɣɤ-plaʁ-laʁ from the root -plaʁ discussed above (the verb in ex:YWGAplaRplaR is ɣɤ-plaʁ- p laʁ ),
and the type II deideophonic verb ɣɤɕtʂaŋlaŋbalance from -ɕtʂaŋ has no correspond type I verb $ $ ɣɤɕtʂaŋɕtʂaŋ despite the fact that a type III pattern ideophone ɕtʂaŋnɤɕtʂaŋbalancing does exist.

An example of an ideophonic root allowing four deideophonic patterns is -ɟɯɣ. The type I verbs ɣɤɟɯɣɟɯɣ (vi) and sɤɟɯɣɟɯɣ (vt), like the corresponding ideophone ɟɯɣnɤɟɯɣ, mean `shake', while the type II verb ɣɤɟɯɣlɯɣ (vi) and sɤɟɯɣlɯɣ (vt) instead mean `wiggle, squirm, creep', expressing a great number of individuals and/or motion in all directions; these verbs are particularly appropriate to refer to insects, snakes or fishes (see for instance ex:pjAGAJWGLWG ), but can also be applied to describe a crowd of people.

exe

tɕe qapri qaɕpa [...] pjɤ-ɣɤ-ɟɯɣlɯɣ ʑo ɕti \\
lnk snake frog ipfv. ifr - deidph: intr -wiggling emph be. aff: fact \\
`There were [many] snakes and frogs wiggling [everywhere].' (2003 kWBRa)
exe

This meaning can also be conveyed by the type IV ideophone ɟɯɣnɤlɯɣ `wiggling'.

The deideophonic functions of ɣɤ- and sɤ- are certainly related to their denominal function. The prefix ɣɤ- is also used to derive dynamic intransitive verbs such as ɣɤwucry (from tɤwucry (n), § sec:denom.intr.GA ), and the meaning of sɤ- as a deideophonic prefix is reminiscent of the causative/instrumental function of sigmatic denominal prefixes (§ sec:denom.sW.caus.instr ).
